evidence_basis.originality_note: Original pulse, string and displacement-table contexts test mapped definition, explanation and graph-construction patterns without copying official wording, values or diagrams.

questions.prompt: At one point, two overlapping waves separately produce displacements of +3.0 mm and -5.0 mm. What is the resultant displacement?
Two identical pulses overlap exactly, with one pulse above equilibrium and the other below equilibrium. Which statement is correct at that instant?

options.A: The resultant is flat because the displacements cancel algebraically.
options.B: The resultant has twice the amplitude because amplitudes are always positive.
options.D: Only the pulse travelling to the right contributes.

questions.prompt: Which procedure correctly finds one point on a resultant displacement graph?

options.A: Add the unsigned amplitudes of the two complete waves.
options.B: Add signed displacements at the same position and instant.
options.C: Add displacements at two different positions on one wave.
options.D: Choose whichever individual displacement has the larger magnitude.
